identity.title: Steering the Herd: A Framework for LLM-based Control of Social Learning

problem.claim: Model and analyze sequential social learning when an information-mediating planner controls signal precision while agents learn from earlier decisions.

contributions.claim: Introduces controlled sequential social learning combining dynamic programming, decentralized actions, and Bayesian belief updates.
Proves value-function convexity and characterizes optimal altruistic and biased planner policies across belief-dependent operating modes.
Studies LLMs acting as both information planner and agents, including strategic steering behavior and deviations from predicted trends.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a new optimization problem for social learning that integrates planner-controlled information precision with decentralized Bayesian learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report convexity of the value function and optimal policies that achieve tradeoffs between planner costs and payoffs from induced choices.
The authors report that, under information parity, no lying or cherry-picking, and full observability, information mediation can shift social welfare substantially in either direction.
The authors report that their LLM-based planner broadly mirrors theoretical steering trends, while key deviations suggest non-Bayesian reasoning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Algorithms mediate information while agents combine private signals with observational learning from peers.
The paper defines a planner-controlled sequential social-learning model in which signal precision is controlled and planner goals may be altruistic or biased.
It formulates a dynamic optimization problem and reports convexity plus belief-dependent optimal investment modes.
For some beliefs, a biased planner intentionally obfuscates agent signals; welfare can move either direction even under transparency constraints.
LLM simulations broadly follow theoretical trends but show deviations attributed by the authors to non-Bayesian reasoning.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates planner objectives, belief ranges, resource-investment modes, and transparency constraints when describing policy consequences.

lessons.interpretation: Explicitly conditioning a policy claim on objectives, state ranges, and governance constraints exposes when the same mechanism can have opposite effects.
lessons.application: State each main result as a conditional map: specify the planner objective, belief region, information constraint, and predicted action or welfare direction.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unnecessary when a study has one fixed objective and operating regime.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative welfare shifts, simulation settings, baselines, or deviation magnitudes.
The conditions and proof details underlying the policy characterization and the meaning of “substantially” are unspecified.
